ceviri.33: Why is the price gap between a ready-made theme and a custom design so wide?
ceviri.34: A template is sold by dividing its development cost among thousands of buyers. On a custom project the team does the analysis, the design and the coding for one client alone. The gap looks wide on day one, but it tends to close over a five-year total cost.
ceviri.35: Does it make sense to start on a ready-made theme and move to a custom design later?
ceviri.36: Yes, and planned properly it is one of the least risky routes there is. The template period works as a kind of market test. You learn which products sell and which campaigns work from real data. When you go into the custom project with that behind you, the requirements list rests on measurement. You don't set budget aside for modules you'll never use, and the payback period shortens. The critical point is catching the moment of transition with a total cost table. And carry the data across to the new project in full.
ceviri.37: How long does a custom design project take to complete?
ceviri.38: It varies with the scope. We share a firm schedule alongside the quote, once the requirements analysis is finished.
ceviri.39: Does a ready-made theme affect search engine performance?
ceviri.40: It can. The code weight of modules you never use can slow the page down. That shows up in ranking signals. With custom development, only the code you need gets written, so managing speed is easier.
ceviri.41: Which items go into the total cost of ownership calculation?
ceviri.42: The setup fee, licence and plugin subscriptions, hosting and the maintenance contract all go in. Customization hours and the rebuild cycle join the list as well. You work out the three- to five-year total of those items separately for each of the two scenarios.
ceviri.43: What happens if we stop paying the licence on a template site?
ceviri.44: The site carries on working, but updates and security patches stop. Over time, plugin incompatibilities build up. That drives up both the repair cost and the risk of data loss.
ceviri.45: How does the maintenance cost work on a custom design?
ceviri.46: The process usually runs on a fixed monthly or annual maintenance contract. The scope covers updates, backups and small enhancements. The risk of a surprise invoice is low.
ceviri.47: Is a custom design essential for a small boutique shop?
ceviri.48: Not essential. If the number of products is limited and traffic doesn't swing much, a template is a budget-friendly place to start. Once the growth signals become clear, planning the move across is enough.

ceviri.62: E-Commerce Website Design: Ready-Made Theme or Custom Design?
ceviri.63: Every SME opening an online shop runs into the same question: ready-made theme or custom design? At that moment, e-commerce website design stops being a visual preference. The decision turns into a cost plan spread across years. The template with the low price tag can swell over time with licence and plugin charges. A custom e-commerce website design, on the other hand, can earn back a high opening budget over the long run. In this article we compare the two approaches along the axis of cost and value. We offer a practical framework that ties your decision to numerical thresholds.
ceviri.64: Two roads to the same destination: the standard mould and the brand-specific build tell different stories in the cost table.
ceviri.66: What Is the Fundamental Difference Between a Ready-Made Theme and a Custom Design?
ceviri.67: A ready-made theme is a rented mould; a custom design is a structure produced from scratch to fit your brand. The difference shows up in ownership and in flexibility. With a template you share the same skeleton with thousands of other shops. On a bespoke project the code, the interface and the decisions about expansion belong entirely to you. That difference in ownership has a direct bearing on every item you will pay for in the years ahead.
ceviri.68: A ready-made theme is a packaged interface produced to be sold to a great many shops. A custom design is a solution coded from scratch for the goals of a single brand. All rights to the code belong to the client. The number of businesses in Türkiye taking this decision is rising fast.
ceviri.70: — ETBİS is Türkiye's central e-commerce information system — puts the number of businesses trading online in the country at 634,611. As the market grows more crowded, the power of e-commerce website design to set you apart turns into a value item that never appears on the price tag.
ceviri.71: Why Doesn't the Cost Comparison End at the Price Tag?
ceviri.72: The price tag only tells you about the day of installation. A template's annual licence renewal and its paid plugins are spread across time. The emergency repair bills paid when something turns out to be incompatible swell the list further. On a custom project the maintenance contract is a single, predictable item. The way to compare the two models soundly is to put the three- to five-year total spend in the same table. Value becomes clear over that longer window.
ceviri.73: What Does a Ready-Made Theme Really Cost?
ceviri.74: The real cost is the compounding total, over the years, of the licence, plugin and customization charges added on top of the opening fee. The developer hours spent making a template resemble the brand hardly ever appear in a budget plan. Once the invisible items are added up, the option everyone took for cheap can turn out dearer than expected in the medium term. That is why the calculation has to be built on the five-year figure rather than day one's.
ceviri.75: The appeal of the template economy is speed: you can be selling within a few days. The price of it is staying tied to a standard mould. The more you want adapted to the brand, the more developer hours grow. A project that starts cheap swells on hourly rates. The code of dozens of modules you never use sits on the site as dead weight. That weight shows up in both the speed and the maintenance bill. We see a similar balance on
ceviri.77: projects too. In e-commerce website design, the customization bill can reach several times the price of the theme itself.
ceviri.78: Which Cost Items Are Hidden in a Template?
ceviri.79: Once you have settled your visual identity with our graphic design team, here are the items that businesses starting their e-commerce website design on a template most often overlook:
ceviri.80: The annual theme licence and update package
ceviri.81: Paid plugin subscriptions and version upgrades
ceviri.83: Repairing the functions that break after a theme update
ceviri.84: The performance work needed for pages that have slowed down
ceviri.85: Most quotation documents never raise the annual total of those five items at all.
ceviri.86: When Is a Custom E-Commerce Website Design a Sensible Investment?
ceviri.87: A custom design is a sensible investment for businesses that are growing, looking for brand distinction and seeing traffic climb. It earns the opening outlay back through a rise in conversion. At small scale, a template may well be enough. As turnover grows, the need for flexibility becomes more decisive than the budget. The decision has to come from scale data, not from taste.
ceviri.88: A custom e-commerce website design is a development process in which every component is built around your business model. The scope runs from the interface right through to the admin panel.
ceviri.89: The Ministry of Trade's outlook report
ceviri.90: shows e-commerce volume passed ₺3 trillion in 2024. The sector's share of gross domestic product came to 6.5%. In a growing pie, shops that look like one another get squeezed into competing on price. A bespoke structure, by contrast, sets your brand apart from the crowd. ceviri.93: What Determines the Return on the Investment?
ceviri.94: Three variables determine the return: conversion rate, basket value and how often people buy again. An e-commerce site whose design has been thought through can produce more orders on the same advertising budget. Visibility in search is part of the equation too.

ceviri.97: How Do You Calculate Total Cost of Ownership?
ceviri.98: Total cost of ownership is the sum of the setup, licence, maintenance, customization and renewal charges. You build the calculation over a three- to five-year window. Businesses that compare that total rather than the one-off price see the real difference between the two models. SMEs that set their e-commerce website design budget this way take the emotion out of the decision.
ceviri.99: Total cost of ownership (TCO) is a financial measure. It covers every cost a system produces from the moment of purchase until it is taken out of service. You can build the calculation in five steps:
ceviri.100: Write down the setup fee: the theme price or the custom project quote.
ceviri.101: Add the recurring costs: licence, plugin subscription, hosting, maintenance contract.
ceviri.102: Forecast the customization hours: multiply the annual developer hours by the hourly rate.
ceviri.103: Allow for the rebuild cycle: decide how many years pass before the current structure is built again from scratch.
ceviri.104: Set the five-year totals of the two scenarios one beneath the other and compare them.
ceviri.106: A recurring cost is, unlike a one-off charge, a payment item that comes round every year. Currency movements shake foreign-currency licences and plugin subscriptions directly. For SMEs planning their budget in lira, that volatility is a serious risk. A fixed maintenance contract, by contrast, gives you predictability.
ceviri.107: The Hidden Item: The Cost of Rebuilding
ceviri.108: Beyond a certain point, template sites usually stop accepting patches. That is when a rebuild comes onto the agenda. Picture a concrete scenario. One day the theme's developer stops supporting updates. The payment plugin doesn't agree with the new version and the basket step throws an error. The only way out is to move the product data and build the shop again from scratch. That move means data migration, training the team, and lost sales. On a custom structure, by contrast, you can renew the existing code in stages. That difference alone can shift the five-year cost balance.

ceviri.111: Which Thresholds Should You Look at When Deciding?
ceviri.112: Take the decision by looking at thresholds: number of products, order volume, campaign intensity and growth target. Starting on a template and moving to a custom structure at a certain scale is a perfectly valid strategy too. What matters is catching the moment of transition with cost data rather than guesswork. If at least two of the signs below apply to you, give the custom solution serious consideration.
ceviri.113: By threshold we mean the concrete indicators that lift the choice out of personal taste and tie it to data.
ceviri.115: — TurkStat is Türkiye's statistical institute — indicates that shopping online is continuing to spread through households. As the base of demand widens, your site sits its scale exam sooner. Watch these indicators:
ceviri.116: The product catalogue passes a few hundred lines and managing variants starts to strain the template.
ceviri.117: On campaign days, traffic climbs to several times its usual level.
ceviri.118: As the number of plugins grows, page speed and the maintenance bill deteriorate together.
ceviri.119: Your brand competes in a segment where looking like everyone else costs you sales.
ceviri.120: If your e-commerce site's design sits below those thresholds, carrying on with a template is a defensible choice on budget grounds.
ceviri.121: How Do You Build the Transition Strategy?
ceviri.122: You build the transition strategy on the sales data gathered during the template period. Record which categories turn over in the early months and which devices the orders come from. When site design in e-commerce is shaped by that data, the hit rate goes up. The budget set aside for a custom e-commerce website design then rests on measurement rather than guesswork.
